verdict.rationale: Apify documents its own Schedules feature, which automatically starts Actors and saved tasks at specific times. Webhooks can chain follow-on Actor runs when a run finishes or fails, and monitoring sends alerts, so background automation is a first-party capability. missing for 10: in-depth documentation of schedule recurrence (cron, timezones), detail on unattended run behavior beyond one-line snippets, and independent or hands-on corroboration of autonomous scheduled runs.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Automatically start Actors and saved tasks at specific times.
you can use webhooks to start another Actor when an Actor run finishes or fails.
Webhooks provide an easy and reliable way to configure the Apify platform to carry out an action (e.g. a HTTP request to another service) when a certain system event
Tasks are saved in the Apify platform and can be run multiple times.
Check the performance of your Actors, validate data quality, and receive alerts.
